title: Americas: beer and spirits
scope: US and Canadian craft breweries (regional, top 200), bourbon and craft whiskey distilleries in KY/TN and beyond, plus the brewery-software incumbents (Ekos, Ollie, Beer30, BrewLedger, Breww, ProBrew) as partner rather than customer targets. Also Latin America: Ambev, Grupo Modelo and the Brazilian and Mexican craft scenes.

title: Americas: wine
scope: Napa, Sonoma, Oregon, Washington and Ontario wineries; Chilean and Argentine export wineries. Premium tier where a small quality gain is worth real money.

title: UK and Ireland
scope: Scotch distilleries (especially the new-wave independents), Irish whiskey, English and Welsh craft brewers, English sparkling wine. Note the SWA net-zero-by-2040 measurement mandate as a live buying trigger.

title: Germany, DACH and the Nordics
scope: German Mittelstand family breweries, Austrian and Swiss producers, Nordic new-wave whisky distilleries (Mackmyra, Stauning and peers), plus equipment vendors (Krones, Anton Paar, ProLeiT) as partner targets.

title: Europe: France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Benelux, CEE
scope: Wine cooperatives and estates, Cognac and Armagnac houses, Belgian and Czech breweries, Polish and Baltic spirits. Co-ops matter most: they aggregate fruit from many growers, so quality variance is their core commercial problem.

title: Japan, Korea and Greater China
scope: Japan's 130+ whisky distilleries and regional sake kura, Korean soju and craft beer, Chinese craft brewers and baijiu distilleries. Flag where a local partner is mandatory rather than optional.

title: Southeast Asia and Oceania
scope: Vietnam (Heineken, Sabeco, Habeco, craft), Thailand, Singapore regional HQs, Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia; Australian and New Zealand wineries and craft brewers.

title: Africa, Middle East and Turkey
scope: South African wine estates and Heineken Beverages, East and West African brewers, North African wine, Gulf non-alcoholic malt producers, Turkish producers. The non-alc malt segment has the same process problems and none of the alcohol politics.

title: Conferences, associations and channel multipliers (global)
scope: Brewing, distilling and wine conferences with dates through 2027-2028; national and regional industry associations; technical institutes; trade press. These are the highest-leverage rows per hour spent, so cover them properly.
